record.category: managed MongoDB-compatible document database (FerretDB proxy over PostgreSQL)

free_tier.stated: A Free Tier is offered for developers, students and small projects; its numeric storage or request allowance is not published on first-party pages. Free Tier instances are temporary and may be stopped or deleted if inactive, and TLS/SSL is not supported on Free Tier instances.
free_tier.notes: The first-party Cloud docs name a Free Tier but publish no storage or request quota; a plan subscription is activated only on approval. A size quoted by third parties is not used here.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no per-object or storage cap is published on the first-party Cloud docs or the signup page
per_object_cap.notes: No numeric cap appears on the first-party pages captured; a value only an approved account would show is not asserted.

retention.stated: Free Tier instances are temporary and may be stopped or deleted if inactive.
retention.notes: The docs give no inactivity threshold in days, so days is null; deletion is conditional on inactivity rather than a fixed countdown.

egress.terms: unverified: no first-party egress allowance, quota or price for FerretDB Cloud is published on the Cloud docs or signup page

record.interface_detail: A MongoDB wire-protocol endpoint reached by a mongodb:// connection string whose username, password and endpoint are shown in the instance dashboard. Free Tier connects without TLS; paid tiers require ?tls=true. A web dashboard manages deployments.
record.tooling: any MongoDB-compatible client (mongosh, MongoDB Compass, official MongoDB drivers)
record.chaining: A hosted FerretDB endpoint is reachable from any MongoDB driver without changing client code; the open-source FerretDB proxy that the user installs and runs on a rented or free machine is the last-resort option if the hosted tier is not approved.

limits.value: Free Tier instances are temporary and may be stopped or deleted if inactive
unverified: no numeric storage or object cap is published for the Free Tier

record.binding_note: No numeric quota is published; the first constraint on a free instance is that it may be stopped or deleted while inactive, and it has no TLS.

identity_cost.detail: FerretDB Cloud signup marks Name, Email, Company Name and Password as required and Company URL as optional, then asks the user to click an email verification link. The docs say the user is notified by email upon approval of the chosen plan. No card, phone or ID document is requested at signup.

record.reliability_note: Free Tier instances are temporary and may be stopped or deleted if inactive; TLS/SSL is not supported on Free Tier, while Pro, Enterprise and Bring Your Own Account Enterprise tiers require TLS.
record.confidence_note: All stated values are from first-party FerretDB documentation and the FerretDB Cloud signup page captured on 2026-11-19. The free-tier allowance is not stated by either source and is left unverified.

evidence.quote: FerretDB Cloud is a managed service that lets you create, deploy, and manage FerretDB instances in the cloud.
evidence.proved: FerretDB Cloud is a hosted managed database service, not self-hosted software

evidence.quote: TLS/SSL connections are not supported in Free tier instances - Ensure to connect without adding (`?tls=true`) to the connection string.
evidence.proved: the Free Tier has no TLS; paid tiers require ?tls=true

evidence.quote: Free Tier instances are temporary and may be stopped or deleted if inactive.
evidence.proved: free instances can be stopped or deleted on inactivity

evidence.quote: You will be notified by email upon approval.
evidence.proved: a subscription plan is activated only after approval
the signup form requires a name
the signup form requires a company name and no card or phone

record.notes: A hosted MongoDB-compatible document database with a Free Tier, but the free instance is temporary, has no TLS, and a plan needs approval. No dollar price and no numeric free allowance are published on first-party pages; the self-hosted open-source FerretDB proxy is the last resort, not the offer this record describes.
